threads.body: `_is_text_part(content)` can partially consume single-pass iterables (e.g., generators) because it calls `all(...)` over `content`; if it returns `False`, the subsequent `_extract_content_parts(content)` iterates the *remaining* items, silently dropping whatever was consumed during `_is_text_part`. It also treats any `Mapping` as an iterable of keys, which is unlikely to be intended for content-part arrays. Consider materializing non-string, non-mapping iterables once and branching on the materialized sequence to avoid data loss and unintended iteration.

replies.body: Good catch — addressed in the latest commit. `content` is now routed through a single `_content_to_parts` helper that materializes non-string, non-mapping iterables exactly once before branching, so single-pass iterables are no longer partially consumed, and mappings keep the previous `_is_text_part` behavior (string-keyed mappings captured as `str(mapping)`) instead of being iterated as content-part arrays. Added unit tests for both cases (generator content and mapping content).

Correction to my earlier reply here: "materialize once" was the wrong fix. The SDK accepts any iterable for `content` and materializes it itself, so consuming a generator inside the instrumentation (which runs before `wrapped()`) drained the caller's input and the SDK sent `content: []`. As of 7d339a8 only `Sequence` content is walked; other iterables are left untouched and simply not captured, and the unit test now asserts the generator is still unconsumed afterwards.

`opentelemetry-util-genai` provides the `image_from_url` helper in `opentelemetry.util.genai.utils` for this exact purpose (it handles external URLs as `UriPart` and base64 data URLs as `BlobPart`). Please reuse `image_from_url(url)` here. `GenericPart` should only be used for provider-specific parts that have no standard semconv representation.

Done in d7e6b9a — `image_url` parts now go through `image_from_url(url)`: an external URL becomes a `UriPart` and a `data:` URL becomes a `BlobPart`.

While at it I mapped the other standard OpenAI parts too, so `GenericPart` is only used for typed parts that have no semconv representation:
- `input_audio` → audio `BlobPart` (mime type derived from `format`)
- `file` → `FilePart` for `file_id`, or a document `BlobPart` for inline `file_data`

Stringifying mappings as `TextPart(content=str(content))` turns arbitrary dicts into malformed text parts like `TextPart(content="{'unexpected': 'shape'}")`.

Similarly, `all(isinstance(item, str) for item in items): return [TextPart(content=str(items))]` produces stringified Python list syntax (`TextPart(content="['a', 'b']")`). Iterables should route through `_extract_content_parts` so string items become individual `TextPart` instances.

replies.body:
Agreed — that was a bad carry-over from the old `_is_text_part` behaviour. Both stringifications are gone in d7e6b9a:
- a bare mapping is treated as a single content part, so `{"type": "text", "text": ...}` becomes a `TextPart` and an untyped dict is dropped instead of becoming a bogus text part;
- string items in a list each become their own `TextPart`.

Everything now routes through one `_convert_content_part` and the iterable is consumed exactly once.

replies.body:
Agreed. There is no size guard anywhere in util-genai and a single clip would be base64-inlined into `gen_ai.input.messages` (a span that large can fail the whole OTLP export batch), so inline audio is no longer captured as of 4f9f343: `input_audio` parts are explicitly skipped, rather than falling through to a `GenericPart` that would have embedded the base64 in `value`, while the text/image parts around them are still captured.

The same argument applies to inline `file_data` documents, so 4b0748a gives them the same treatment: `file` parts are captured only when they carry a `file_id` (as a `FilePart`), and inline `file_data` is skipped. For what it's worth, the anthropic instrumentation is the one place that inlines document bytes today; google-genai records documents as a `UriPart` reference only. @lmolkova, if "and others" in your review was meant to include inline audio and documents as a `BlobPart`, just say so and I'll restore those mappings.

The remaining inline case is data-URL images, which come from util-genai's `image_from_url` (as @lmolkova asked for above). I left that as-is since it's shared util behaviour rather than something this PR decides; if those shouldn't be inlined either, that seems like a util-genai-level call.
